$comment: Single-node readiness ledger for the hardware proof-of-concept.
This file is the CHECKED-IN, DIFFABLE record of what the cluster manifests
claim versus what one box can actually deliver. The auditor fails on DRIFT
away from this record: a new app-of-apps identity collision, a new workload
declaring redundancy it cannot have on nodeCount nodes, or a PVC total that
outgrows nodeDiskGib. Every acknowledgement below is DEBT with a reason and
STATUS: awaiting maintainer sign-off on nodeDiskGib (see below).
Dejan 2026-08-14 - drafted from a live single-node bring-up, not from a plan.
2026-08-21 - nodeDiskGib is NO LONGER the auditor's only comparator, because
it never was a measurement. The `capacity-provenance` check compares the same
declared totals against MEASURED hardware read off the checked-in ClusterNode
registrations under maintainers/*/cluster-nodes/*/node.yaml, and it REFUSES
(exits 1) when no registration carries a measurable spec.hardware.storage.
The nodeDiskGib budget line is still checked and is still useful as the
procurement target - it is simply now labelled ASPIRATIONAL in the output,
which is what it always was.
$comment_activeStorageProfile: Which rung of full-ai-cluster/k8s/storage-profiles.json THIS deployment runs.
REQUIRED - readLedger refuses a ledger without it, because a default rung
would let the storage-profile check report agreement with a profile nobody
selected, which is a check that cannot fail.
The ladder, and the box each rung needs (Longhorn keeps 25% of a disk
minimally-available by chart default, plus ~30 GiB of OS root):
minimal    200 GiB declared    172 GiB at bring-up   ~300 GiB box
standard   595 GiB declared    467 GiB at bring-up   ~825 GiB box
large     1599 GiB declared   1099 GiB at bring-up   ~2.2 TiB box
`large` is ACTIVE because `large` is byte-for-byte what the manifests already
declared before the ladder existed - naming the status quo is not the same as
endorsing it. It does NOT fit node-ad1efd, which is why the capacity shortfall
below is still carried as debt.
TO SHRINK THIS CLUSTER TO ITS MEASURED HARDWARE, two edits and no new debt:
bun src/Core.TypeScript/cluster/storage-profiles.ts --profile standard --apply
set activeStorageProfile to "standard" here, and DELETE the
acknowledgedCapacityShortfall entry - at 595 GiB against 1047 GiB measured
there is nothing left to acknowledge.
That is the whole point of the ladder: the 552 GiB shortfall stopped being a
procurement question and became a one-line choice, without anything being
silently dropped - every cut's cost is written out per claim in the catalogue.
$comment_nodeDiskGib: Usable disk per node, in GiB, dedicated to the replicated-storage class.
DERIVED, NOT GUESSED. Running the auditor prints the sum of every declared
PVC capacity x pod count. Measured 2026-08-21 on the live tree:
longhorn         1599 GiB   (profile "large", the checked number)
longhorn         1409 GiB   (the extractor's independent reading; it
cannot see mimir's chart-default pod counts
and mis-attributes redis master's - kept as
a cross-check, not as the answer)
zeta-local-path   103 GiB
(the 1499/73 GiB figures recorded here on 2026-08-14 moved when vault
dropped to replicas=1 in PR #13062; the auditor prints the live numbers,
this comment is a dated snapshot and will drift again.)
so a node that syncs the whole `large` catalogue needs ~1.6 TiB of declared
PVC, i.e. ~2.2 TiB of disk once Longhorn's 25% minimally-available reserve
and the OS root are paid for.
2048 is the next standard NVMe size above the OLD 1.4 TiB reading and is now
slightly UNDER what `large` needs - which is itself an argument for running
`standard` rather than buying to fit `large`. It is NOT a measurement of
the box Aaron has today - it is the requirement the manifests imply, and it
is the number that needs a yes/no before hardware is bought. Because it is
not a measurement, it is not what the auditor VERIFIES against; see
$comment_acknowledgedCapacityShortfall.
Measured counter-example (2026-08-14, kind 0.31.0 on podman/applehv, one
node, 100 GB disk): the catalogue oversubscribed the disk ~15x. Longhorn
reported ReplicaSchedulingFailure 'insufficient storage;precheck new replica
failed', volumes went robustness=faulted, and cockroachdb-0/1/2 never left
Init:0/1 with AttachVolume.Attach failed 'volume is not ready for workloads'.
That is what an under-budgeted node looks like.
$comment_nodeCount: Nodes in the PoC cluster. One box today. Raise this as workers join; every
acknowledgedFalseRedundancy entry below should be re-examined when it does,
because most of them stop being false at nodeCount >= 3.
$comment_acknowledgedFalseRedundancy: Workloads that declare replicas > nodeCount WITHOUT hard anti-affinity, so
Kubernetes co-schedules every replica onto the one node. They come up green;
the redundancy is nominal and the failure domain is a single disk. Listing
one here does NOT make it safe - it makes it stated, so nobody demos it as
high availability.
full-ai-cluster/cockroachdb  3 Raft members, chart default podAntiAffinity
type=soft. Observed co-scheduled on one node.
full-ai-cluster/vault        server.ha.replicas=3 with raft.enabled=true.
Same shape: Raft quorum, one failure domain.
full-ai-cluster/nats         JetStream cluster.replicas=3. Same shape.
full-ai-cluster/redis        replica.replicaCount=2. Async replication, so
no quorum to lose - but no redundancy either.
full-ai-cluster/platform     examples/gmod-server.yaml replicas=2. A sample
workload, not part of the PoC critical path.
full-ai-cluster/kubevirt     virt-operator Deployment replicas=2, from the
VENDORED upstream kubevirt-operator.yaml
(v1.8.4, line 8493). Upstream ships 2 for
control-plane HA; on one node both co-schedule.
NOT edited down to 1 on purpose: that manifest
is vendored byte-for-byte so it stays 1:1 with
what runs, and node-5b2dfa really does run two
virt-operator pods today. Editing it would make
the checked-in copy diverge from the cluster it
documents, which is a worse lie than this one.
Resolves at nodeCount >= 2 with no code change.
Removing an entry from this list is the fix, and the fix is one of: drop to
nodeCount replicas (honest single node), set hard anti-affinity (the shortfall
becomes visible Pending pods), or add nodes.
$comment_acknowledgedCapacityShortfall: MEASURED oversubscription, carried as debt until 5.1 of
docs/design/2026-08-21-the-zeta-bootstrap-usb-full-design-document.md is decided.
Owner: Aaron (it is a procurement/product call, not an engineering one).
The arithmetic, 2026-08-21, all of it re-checkable by running the auditor:
declared  longhorn PVCs, profile "large"              1599 GiB
measured  node-ad1efd, /dev/nvme0n1 931.5G            931.5 GiB
+ /dev/sda      115.5G            115.5 GiB
every block device on the node   1047.0 GiB
shortfall                                              552 GiB  (1.53x)
THE DECLARED SIDE GREW BY 190 GiB AND NOTHING WAS ADDED TO THE CLUSTER.
It was 1409 GiB here on 2026-08-21 because that was what the auditor's YAML
extractor derived, and the extractor was wrong in both directions:
+200  mimir. mimir-distributed 5.5.1 ships ingester.replicas=3 AND
zone-aware replication over 3 zones for BOTH ingester and
store_gateway; templates/_helpers.tpl:568 computes
replicaPerZone = ceil(replicas / zones), so ingester renders 3 pods
(1 per zone) and store_gateway renders 3 as well (ceil(1/3) = 1 per
zone). 6 PVCs of 50Gi where the extractor counted 2. None of those
counts appear in our YAML, so no reader of our YAML can find them.
-10  redis. The extractor's nearest-enclosing-replicas heuristic handed
the MASTER claim the neighbouring replica.replicaCount=2; bitnami
redis with architecture: replication runs exactly one master.
1409 + 200 - 10 = 1599. The 1409 was not a smaller disk requirement, it was
a less complete reading of the same manifests - which is why the number now
comes from full-ai-cluster/k8s/storage-profiles.json, where every pod count
carries its provenance, and the extractor's independent reading is kept as a
cross-check rather than as the answer.
Provenance of the measured side: maintainers/Addisons820/cluster-nodes/
node-ad1efd/node.yaml, written by zeta-install.sh from
`lsblk -ndo NAME,SIZE,TYPE -e7` on that node during a real metal boot
(2026-06-09) and committed by a self-registration PR. lsblk's human sizes
are BINARY, so 931.5G is 931.5 GiB and compares directly to Kubernetes Gi.
The bound is deliberately GENEROUS: it counts /dev/sda, which is very
possibly the USB stick, and it reserves nothing for the ESP, the root
filesystem, swap, or Longhorn's own storageReserved. So exceeding it is
proven oversubscription and no reading of the hardware rescues it; NOT
exceeding it would prove nothing. The inference convicts, never acquits.
Two of the four registered nodes (maximdolphin's node-f82aa6 and
node-5b2dfa) record NO hardware.storage at all - the post-boot
self-register path never captured it. They are excluded from the bound and
printed as unmeasured rather than counted as zero.
WHY THE KEY CARRIES BOTH NUMBERS: acknowledging the bare storage class
would make this check unfalsifiable - any later PVC growth, or a smaller
node joining, would be silently absorbed. Pinned, every movement of either
side goes red and has to be re-stated deliberately. In particular this
entry STOPS BEING VALID the moment a 2 TB node is registered, which is
exactly when someone should be deleting it.
Removing this entry is the fix, and the fix is now CHEAP - which it was not
when this comment was first written. Switching activeStorageProfile from
"large" to "standard" (595 GiB) and running
`storage-profiles.ts --profile standard --apply` clears the shortfall
outright, with every cut's cost written out claim by claim in the catalogue.
The other options remain: buy the disk, or split storage-heavy apps onto a
big-disk worker. All are 5.1 options.
WHAT THE BRING-UP NUMBER DOES AND DOES NOT BUY. Of the 1599 GiB, 500 GiB
provisions nothing on a fresh sync: ollama (200) and vllm (200) are
zeta.io/sync-policy: manual so ArgoCD never applies them, and
arc-runner-set/model-cache-pvc.yaml (100) is applied by NOTHING - the root
App-of-Apps includes only '{*/Application.yaml,Application.yaml}' and
arc-runner-set's own Application sources a remote Helm chart rather than
that git path. So bring-up provisions 1099 GiB. That is still 52 GiB over
the measured bound, so the honest-bring-up reading does not rescue the fit,
and it is NOT why this entry can be smaller: Longhorn's StorageClass is
volumeBindingMode Immediate, so those 500 GiB land in full the moment anyone
syncs the apps. Convicting on the bring-up subset would be a gate that
passes today and fails the first time someone acts on it.
NOTE: the UNVERIFIED case is not acknowledgeable here and must not become
so. A shortfall you can see is debt; an absent comparator is an absent
check, and an exemption for it would be the vacuity this ledger exists to
prevent.
$comment_acknowledgedRootAppDuplicates: argocd/zeta-root is declared TWICE with two different spec.source.path values:
Kubernetes has exactly one object at that identity. Both roots carry
prune: true + selfHeal: true, so whichever is applied last owns the name and
prunes the other tree's entire child Application graph.
This is the mechanical reason the two trees cannot both be pointed at one
cluster, and the reason 'run the live test against both trees' is not a
cheap option. Tracked for consolidation; delete this entry when one tree
